name: LeDex: Training LLMs to Better Self-Debug and Explain Code
authors: Nan Jiang et al. (Purdue University; AWS AI Labs; University of Virginia)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, pp. 35517-35543)
reflection_type: learned-critic-model (trained reflective behavior via SFT+RL; the model learns to produce an explanation/critique of its own wrong code, with a trained reward signal for explanation quality). Feedback at training time is tool-verified (unit-test execution).
feedback_source: external-tool (Python interpreter / unit-test execution verification) used both to filter the training trajectories and as the unit-test passing-rate component of the RL reward; explanation quality measured via RoBERTa sentiment/embedding similarity. At inference, the model conditions on unit-test execution feedback (error message or failed test case).
iteration_structure: iterative-refine: code generation followed by self-debugging that explains the wrong code then refines it; can iterate for multiple rounds (evaluated up to 3 rounds of refinement) until a correct solution or max iterations is reached.
reflection_object: Primarily the output content (the generated wrong code) plus the reasoning chain: the model produces a natural-language explanation/diagnosis of the wrong code (CoT-style) and then a refinement. The corrective signal is baked into model weights (SFT + RL fine-tuning), so the durable change is to model weights, while the in-context object reflected upon is the buggy code + execution feedback.
requires_training: nested-RL+SFT: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on automatically collected and execution-verified explanation+refinement trajectories, followed by reinforcement learning (PPO) on both success and failure trajectories.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (unit-test passing rate S_ut and CodeBLEU similarity S_cb to verified correct refinements) combined with a learned-embedding explanation reward (RoBERTa cosine/sentiment similarity S_ex of the explanation to verified-correct explanations). Refinement reward R(r) and explanation reward R(e) are designed and applied separately within PPO.
distillation_target: model-weights: explanation+refinement capability is distilled (from a teacher LLM such as GPT-3.5-Turbo, CodeLlama-34B, or the model itself via self-bootstrap) into the student model's weights through SFT and then sharpened with RL.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered: the reflective behavior (explain-then-refine chain) is scaffolded via prompt design and an explicitly engineered training pipeline (data collection, verification, SFT, and a hand-designed PPO reward), not RL-emergent in the R1 'aha-moment' sense.
memory_type: none (no external memory store at inference; experience is internalized into weights). Within an episode the chat history holds the buggy code and execution feedback as a short-term scratchpad/context.
memory_persistence: within-episode for the in-context buggy code/feedback; learned experience persists in weights cross-task (the fine-tuned model carries debugging ability across all test problems).
memory_curation_mechanism: retrieval-gated / execution-verified filtering of training data: candidate explanations and refinements are kept only if the refinement passes all unit tests (execution verification); explanations are kept when paired with a correct refinement. There is no runtime episodic memory to curate.
error_localization_granularity: response-level / holistic: the model explains and refines the whole wrong solution conditioned on the failing test or error message, rather than localizing to a specific code block or token. (Unit-test passing rate gives outcome-level granularity in the reward.)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task at inference (refine a single task's solution using its own execution feedback, optionally over multiple rounds); inter-task at training (debugging skill learned from many tasks transfers to new held-out tasks via weights).
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision: after an initial solution fails the unit tests, the model produces an explanation and a revised solution; supports iterative post-hoc refinement over multiple rounds rather than mid-trajectory in-flight correction.
task_domains: code (program synthesis / code generation and automated self-debugging/repair for Python programming tasks).
benchmarks: Evaluation: MBPP, HumanEval, MBPP+, HumanEval+ (pass@k and success refinement rate). Training data sources: MBPP training set (374 problems), APPS training set (5,000 problems), and CodeContests.
headline_result: On three open-source backbones (StarCoder-15B, CodeLlama-7B, CodeLlama-13B), SFT improves pass@1 by up to 15.92% and pass@10 by up to 9.30% across four benchmarks; RL on top of SFT adds up to 3.54% pass@1 and 2.55% pass@10. Success refinement rate improves by up to ~10.15% (SFT) with up to a further 3.62% from RL.
baselines: Prompting-based self-debugging on the same open-source backbones: 'Refine' (directly ask for a refinement) and 'Expl. + Refine' (ask for an explanation of the wrong code then refine, CoT-style); GPT-3.5-Turbo serves as a strong reference/teacher (e.g., on explanation quality and refinement rate). Prior training-based approaches discussed: ILF, CYCLE, Self-Edit, OpenCodeInterpreter, EURUS.
gains_vs_baseline: vs prompting baseline: StarCoder-15B SFT (Expl.+Refine) +15.92% pass@1 and +6.30% pass@10 on MBPP&HumanEval (+14.13% pass@1, +9.30% pass@10 on MBPP+&HumanEval+); CodeLlama-7B SFT +14.41% pass@1; CodeLlama-13B SFT +12.23% pass@1. RL vs SFT: e.g., CodeLlama-13B +3.54% pass@1 on MBPP+&HumanEval+; StarCoder-15B +2.43% pass@1 / +2.55% pass@10 on MBPP&HumanEval. Success refinement rate (avg over 4 benchmarks): StarCoder-15B from 6.41-6.90% (prompting) to 16.27-16.56% (SFT, +9.37-10.15%) to 17.50-17.59% (RL); CodeLlama-13B up to 23.50% (RL).
compute_cost_profile: Training cost: SFT for 2 epochs (batch size 128, lr 2e-5, AdamW, 500-step warmup, cosine decay) plus PPO RL (lr 2e-6, batch size 64, TRL library), all on 8x NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs. Data-collection cost: sample 20 solutions per training problem (temperature 1.0) plus explanation+refinement generations from a teacher LLM, filtered by execution. Inference cost: roughly one extra generation per wrong solution per refinement round (multi-round iterative refinement multiplies calls by number of rounds, evaluated up to 3 rounds); explanation+refinement adds tokens vs direct refinement.
known_limitations: Reliance on specific teacher LLMs for data collection (GPT-3.5-Turbo, CodeLlama-34B, or self; other/smaller/mixed LLMs unexplored). Only two self-debug prompt types tested (direct refine; explain-then-refine); broader prompt strategies not explored. Requires unit tests / execution environment to verify training trajectories and supply RL reward, so depends on access to test cases. Demonstrated on relatively small Python benchmarks (MBPP/HumanEval and their + variants); not validated on repository-level or other languages.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier (and partially oracle-label at training): unit-test execution verifies refinements both for data filtering and as the RL reward; ground-truth correct refinements are used to compute the CodeBLEU similarity reward component. At inference, the model relies on provided unit-test execution feedback (error messages/failed test cases) to drive refinement, so it is not intrinsic-only.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive: training (SFT and RL) produces consistent pass@k and success-refinement-rate gains over prompting baselines on small open-source LLMs, including with execution-verified feedback. The gains are largely attributable to internalizing the explain-then-refine skill, but the method still depends on unit-test execution feedback rather than improving correction without any external signal.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report confidence calibration; it focuses on pass@k, success refinement rate, and human/GPT-4-rated explanation quality).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (LeDex is a training method for self-debugging, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis benchmark; it does produce natural-language explanations of why code is wrong, but does not formally classify failure modes or attribute a responsible agent/step in a multi-agent taxonomy sense).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets incorrect code generated by small open-source LLMs (logic/runtime/test-failing bugs) and the related failure mode of superficial or low-quality self-reflection: prompting-only self-debug on small LLMs barely refines wrong solutions (e.g., StarCoder-15B refines only 4.43% of MBPP wrong solutions vs 28.90% for GPT-3.5-Turbo); LeDex trains the model to produce useful explanations and effective refinements, mitigating ineffective/shallow self-correction.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Releases an automatically collected, execution-verified code explanation + refinement training dataset (e.g., with GPT-3.5-Turbo: 13,735 verified correct explanation+refinement pairs - 2,203 MBPP, 6,419 APPS, 5,113 CodeContests). [uncertain] whether the dataset/code/checkpoints were publicly released with a downloadable artifact link.
builds_on: Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug (Chen et al., 2024); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023); Self-Edit and CYCLE (training-based code refinement); ILF / Imitation learning from Language Feedback (training with language feedback); OpenCodeInterpreter and EURUS (multi-turn interaction SFT datasets); PPO (Schulman et al.) via the TRL library; backbones StarCoder and CodeLlama; CodeBLEU and RoBERTa for reward components.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited/contrasted as a training-based self-debug baseline by TGPR: Tree-Guided Policy Refinement for Robust Self-Debugging of LLMs (arXiv:2510.06878); ReflexiCoder (RL self-reflection/self-correction for code, contrasts LeDex's external-oracle dependence); Revisit Self-Debugging with Self-Generated Tests for Code Generation (ACL 2025); DePro: Understanding the Role of LLMs in Debugging Competitive Programming Code (arXiv:2603.19399).
reasoning_model_native: no: LeDex predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; it explicitly trains explain-then-refine behavior into small non-reasoning code LLMs (StarCoder-15B, CodeLlama-7B/13B) via SFT+PPO rather than relying on emergent reflective reasoning.
on_policy_distillation_link: Related to skill distillation: LeDex distills explanation+refinement skill from a teacher (GPT-3.5-Turbo / CodeLlama-34B) or self-bootstrapped data into the student via SFT, then does on-policy RL (PPO) on the model's own generated success/failure trajectories with execution-verified rewards. This SFT-distillation-then-on-policy-RL recipe is adjacent to on-policy distillation / skill-optimization, though the paper does not frame it using the on-policy-distillation terminology.
sample_efficiency: Data scale: 20 sampled solutions per training problem (temperature 1.0) over MBPP-train (374), APPS-train (5,000), and CodeContests, yielding e.g. 13,735 execution-verified explanation+refinement pairs (GPT-3.5-Turbo); SFT for 2 epochs. At inference, iterative refinement evaluated up to 3 rounds, with most gains realized after the first refinement round. Exact PPO rollout/step counts are [uncertain].
